summary: According to a small computer model rather than human tests, Sitaxentan received a high risk score of 78 for the liver and a low risk score of 31 for the heart [M]. The drug was pulled from the market worldwide starting in 2010 due to liver harm [3]. In addition, multiple clinical studies were stopped early on December 9, 2010, because of safety concerns involving new signs of liver injury [5][6][7].
